<reason>B won a competitive debate by staying on the motion’s actual decision rule: who loses when the reviewer cannot tell. The presumption-as-burden-shift, the mitigation path (trustee, offtake, divest-on-trigger), and the irreversibility comparison (stalled ore vs sunk rival control) remained live after full exchange. A damaged B’s original “cheap error is a lower sale price” claim and landed the stronger host-license / third-country / scarce-capital story, but never neutralized the fork or the hard case of a compelled firm demanding full control. A’s closing also tried to recast the motion as “does a default no ship metal,” which is weighing, not the written presumption question. B’s clipped first rebuttal is a real execution cost, but later speeches recovered and made the vote easier.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s Rebuttal 2 fork: if title does not control flows the block is cheap, and if losing the bidder kills the mine then title is a supply lever state acquirers pay for—plus the A1 answer that compulsion can be structurally severed rather than treated as a ban.</best_rebuttal>
